propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, and peer-state delegation with no cohesive ownership of safety rules.
Production code mutates inner entries returned by shallow all_bindings() query, risking regressions in crash recovery, index lag, identity, serialization, and selective publication.
Decompose BindingStore behind a unified facade into three internal owners: repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, and recovery; preserve public signatures and byte serialization.
Durable tombstone is authoritative retirement intent; live forward/reverse pairs are removed only when tombstone and both identities agree, and only explicit unretire revokes intent.
Live recovery must run after staleness validation but not interleave new liveness evidence with completion; create and retirement-completion recovery are idempotent and keyed by exact identity match.
Load, check, dry-run, preview, and selection operations must never trigger recovery writes; only validated write-bearing operations may repair interrupted retirements.
